texts.preamble: In Re vs Sh. Sumit Tiwari on 31 January, 2017 In The Court Of Sh. Ashu Garg, Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate - Ii (New Delhi), Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Cc No. 90/11 Unique Case Id No. 02403R0039712011 Date of Institution: 09.05.2011 Date of reserving judgement: 31.01.2017 Date of pronouncement: 31.01.2017 In re: Delhi Administration / Food Inspector Department of Pfa, Govt. of Nct of Delhi A-20, Lawrence Road Industrial Area, Delhi-110035 ... texts.facts: The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (Pfa Act), wherein it is alleged that the accused had sold misbranded food in violation of Section 2 (ix)(d) and (e) of PFA Act, as punishable under Section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act. 2. As per the complaint, on 31.10.2010, the food officials including Food Inspector (FI) Geet Ram and Field Assistant (FA) Balwant Shah under the supervision of Local Health Authority (LHA)/SDM Smt. Usha Chaturvedi reached at the premises of M/s. Tiwari Sweets at 27/37, Gali No.9, Vishwas Nagar, Delhi-110032, where the accused in the capacity of vendor-cum-proprietor was found conducting the business of various food articles, including 'Patisa', which was found stored for sale for human consumption, lying in an open tray bearing no label declaration. The food officials lifted the sample the said food article consisting of 1500 gm of Patisa ready for sale. It was divided into three parts as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules and separately packed and sealed. Necessary documents were prepared at the spot including the vendor's receipt and panchanama. Price of the sample was paid to the vendor. One counterpart of the sample was deposited with the Public Analyst (PA) and remaining two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA. Vide report dated 06.12.2010, the PA reported that the sample was misbranded as it showed presence of synthetic which was not declared as one of the ingredients. Based on the report In Re vs Sh. Sumit Tiwari on 31 January, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82354384/ 1 of PA, investigation was carried out by the Food Inspector as per the instructions of the SDM/LHA. After obtaining due sanction of the Director, PFA, the present complaint came to be filed against the accused for violation of the section 2(ix)(d) and (e), as punishable under Section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act for selling misbranded food. 3. Since the complaint was filed by a public servant in writing, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 09.05.2011. Based on the report of PA, notice of accusation under section 251 CrPC was framed vide order dated 25.11.2011 against the accused for commission of offence under Section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act being in violation of Section 2(ix)(e) of PFA Act, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. No notice/charge was framed for violation of section 2(ix)(d) of the Act, though the complaint was filed alleging its violation as well. 4. At the trial, the prosecution examined four witnesses in support of its case. PW-1 FI Jeet Ram, PW-2 Smt. Usha Trivedi, PW-3 FI Balwant Shah were the part of the team that had visited the premises of accused and lifted the sample of Patisa lying in an open tray bearing no label or declaration. These witnesses deposed about the sample proceedings conducted by them on 31.10.2010 and narrated the steps undertaken by them, including disclosing their identity, lifting 1500 gms of Patisa, breaking it into smallest possible pieces with the help of a clean and dry knife, mixing them and dividing the same in three counterparts by putting them in three clean and dry sample glass bottles, adding 40 drops of formalin in each bottle, separately packing, fastening, marking and sealing them. A sum of Rs. 225/- was paid to the vendor as price of the sample vide vendor's receipt Ex. PW-1/ A. Notice in Form-VI Ex. PW-1/B and Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C were prepared at the spot. Raid report Ex. PW- 1/D was also prepared by the FI. One counterpart was deposited with the PA vide receipt Ex. PW-1 / E and remaining two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA vide receipt Ex. PW-1/F on the next working day. PA report Ex. PW-1/G was received opining the sample to be misbranded. Further investigation was carried out during which letter Ex. PW-1/H was written to vendor accused but it was not replied. Letter Ex. PW-1/I was written to STO and its reply Ex. PW-1/J was received. Further investigation was conducted by PW-4 FI M.K.Gupta. After completion of investigation, consent for prosecution Ex. PW-2/A was taken from the Director, PFA, after which the complaint Ex. PW-2/B was filed and intimation letter Ex. PW-4/A was served upon the accused personally against acknowledgement. These witnesses were duly cross examined by the Ld. Defence Counsel, wherein they denied that the accused was falsely implicated. 5. Statement of the accused was recorded under section 313 CrPC on 10.08.2015 wherein he denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Accused accepted the proceedings dated 31.10.2010 but claimed that no effort was made to join public witnesses. He questioned the PA report and claimed that he did not put any colour in the patisa and had used haldi powder. He did not lead any evidence in defence despite opportunity.
texts.arguments: 6. It is in these circumstances, Ld. SPP for the complainant has argued that the complainant has been able to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt, as all the witnesses have supported its case and there is no contradiction in their testimony. It is submitted that the accused has failed to rebut the findings as given by the PA. In Re vs Sh. Sumit Tiwari on 31 January, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82354384/ 2 7. On the other hand, Ld. Defence Counsel for the accused has submitted that the prosecution case fails on technical grounds. Ld. Counsel for accused has submitted that there is no violation of section 2(ix)(e) of PFA Act as there was no false claim made anywhere by the accused. It is submitted that no charge has been framed against the accused for violation of section 2(ix)(d) which pertains to colouring, flavouring, coating or polishing the food article. It is also pointed out that the quantity of the food colour tartrazine has been found to be only 15.22 ppm which is well within permissible limits of 100 ppm.

texts.respondent_arguments: Ld. Counsel for accused has submitted that there is no violation of section 2(ix)(e) of PFA Act as there was no false claim made anywhere by the accused. It is submitted that no charge has been framed against the accused for violation of section 2(ix)(d) which pertains to colouring, flavouring, coating or polishing the food article. It is also pointed out that the quantity of the food colour tartrazine has been found to be only 15.22 ppm which is well within permissible limits of 100 ppm.
